steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: Recruit, appoint or assign the multidisciplinary capability from September through November 2026 and establish its leadership, decision rights, working model and initial product pipeline. Define how product management, service design, user research, software development, data, integration, architecture, security, accessibility, change and service management will work with King’s Edge product owners and students. Bring the core team into place during November so initial product-definition work can begin in parallel while mobilisation is completed, with the team ready for full delivery from December 2026.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide product management, architecture governance and institutional prioritisation across the shared capability and its 4.1.2 and 4.1.4 demand.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The team may receive conflicting demand or build outside agreed institutional guardrails.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide Azure and DevOps support, data and integration expertise, and scheduled security, identity, privacy and accessibility assurance.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Delivery may be delayed or create services that cannot be integrated, assured or supported.

existingCapacity.contribution: Define live support, monitoring, incident, change and service-ownership arrangements as capabilities move into operation.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Products may launch without a credible operating model.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: Indicative £201,000 in constant 2026 prices for November 2026 to June 2027.
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Two full-stack engineers, one product and experience designer and one agile delivery manager, including hands-on technical leadership within the engineering capacity.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The institution will not establish the in-house development capability required by 4.1.2 and 4.1.4.

newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Covers platform consumption, standard equipment and tooling, and targeted migration, assurance and testing support. It assumes maximum use of existing institutional licences, specialists and standard provision.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The team may lack the platform and targeted specialist support needed to put its work safely into live operation.

enablingConditions.condition: Approve the first-year team shape and recruitment route in time for recruitment to begin in September 2026.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with King’s Edge sponsorship
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The core team will not be available in November.

enablingConditions.condition: Assign named existing IT contributors with protected availability and decision rights.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Existing capacity may remain inaccessible through competing demand queues.

enablingConditions.condition: Operate one prioritised product pipeline across 4.1.2, 4.1.3 and 4.1.4, with all shared staffing and delivery investment held under 4.1.3.
enablingConditions.owner: King’s Edge Portfolio Board and Digital and IT
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Capacity may be fragmented or double-counted.

enablingConditions.condition: Validate the cost envelopes through a costed solution design and confirmed institutional licence and platform arrangements.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The budget may not reflect the actual operating model.

steps.title: Put the Azure delivery foundations into operation
steps.summary: Establish the Azure environments, hosting model, development and deployment pipelines, source-control and release practices, testing and assurance gates, monitoring, logging, recovery, documentation, design and accessibility standards, API and integration conventions, privacy and security controls, and proportionate AI-assurance approach needed to develop student-facing capabilities quickly without creating unsupported or non-compliant prototypes. Begin this work as the core team becomes available during November and complete the delivery foundations by the end of February 2027.

steps.title: Prove the route from prototype to supported service
steps.summary: Use the first King’s Edge releases to run repeated end-to-end delivery cycles: understand and prioritise a need with business users and students, prototype and test a response, develop it within the shared architecture, complete security, accessibility, data and operational assurance, release it into controlled live use, evaluate it, and either harden it for continued service or conclude it cleanly before it creates an unmanaged long-term commitment.

newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Retains the first-year pod and adds one full-stack or integration engineer and 0.5 FTE quality engineering and test automation.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The team may lack the resilience to operate live services while expanding the wider Hub.

newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Covers live platform consumption and only those specialist integration, assurance, research and adoption costs that cannot be absorbed through existing institutional capacity.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Operating costs may displace planned product delivery.

enablingConditions.condition: Reset the Year 2 profile against the confirmed roadmap and actual platform consumption.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT product leadership with King’s Edge Portfolio Board
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The resource profile may not match the confirmed pipeline.

steps.title: Make the product pipeline and support model routine
steps.summary: Confirm the ongoing backlog, prioritisation, discovery, release, support, incident, maintenance, documentation and ownership arrangements for the Student Experience Hub. Establish a reliable delivery cadence, a transparent route for new demand, clear acceptance criteria for moving from experiment to service, and a practical handover or enduring-ownership model for capabilities that have been hardened.

steps.title: Scale the product capability across the student app roadmap
steps.summary: Apply the established operating model and reusable technical foundations to a growing portfolio of student journeys. Increase throughput while preserving continuous user involvement, coherent architecture, shared components, appropriate assurance and sustainable ownership, and use evidence from delivery to refine team roles, governance, methods and the balance between rapid product work and enterprise hardening.

newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Capacity may taper before the wider Hub has completed its principal transition work.

newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The final integration and transition may not be completed safely.

enablingConditions.condition: Reset the final-year profile against actual platform consumption and the confirmed remaining roadmap.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The budget may not match the remaining work.

steps.title: Embed the team as an enduring institutional capability
steps.summary: Establish the multidisciplinary team, its funding and governance, technical platform, service interfaces and product practices as a sustained institutional capability for continuous improvement of the Student Experience Hub. Ensure the team can respond to new priorities without reverting to disconnected local builds, separate procurements or prototypes that cannot be secured, supported and maintained.
